sections.h2: What drives a sale in East Hempfield
sections.html:
East Hempfield is a suburban township just west of Lancaster city. Three local facts decide what you take home: a countywide reassessment now in progress, the Hempfield School District's rate, which is the biggest slice of the bill, and a township transfer tax.

The township shares the Lancaster mailing designation with five other suburbs, so plenty of East Hempfield houses carry a Lancaster address. Within its lines are Landisville, Mechanicsville, Rohrerstown, Bamford, Centerville, Chestnut Ridge, Donerville, Chestnut View and Wheatland, plus a piece of Salunga.

Owners occupy 72.5 percent of homes here. The midpoint owned home is worth $360,500, midpoint rent runs $1,383 a month and midpoint household income is $99,384. Population was an estimated 27,287 on July 1, 2025, compared with 26,304 in 2020.

County and township real estate taxes in East Hempfield are collected by the Lancaster County Treasurer. The Hempfield School District sends its own bill. Its 2026-27 rate is 19.8786 mills, a 4.1 percent increase over last year.

Anything unpaid after December 31 moves to the Lancaster County Tax Claim Bureau. Call that office for questions about delinquent accounts.

School tax certifications come from the Lancaster County Tax Collection Bureau. Email your request and include the owner's name, the street address, the 13-digit parcel number, the settlement date and an email address or fax number for the reply. Mail a $25 check made out to LCTCB Real Estate Tax Group along with it. Leave out any of these items and the request is returned, which can push back closing, so send it well ahead.

On top of the Commonwealth's 1 percent, the township charges 1 percent of the property's value for its general purposes. It adopted the ordinance in 1987 under the state Tax Reform Code and the Local Tax Enabling Act. Payment is due when the deed goes in for recording, and in any case within 30 days after the document is accepted.

Buyer and seller are jointly liable under the Department of Revenue's rules. The ordinance exempts several transfers, such as a transfer to an heir from a decedent and some transfers to the trustee of an ordinary trust, as long as the Recorder of Deeds receives a copy of the trust instrument. Family transfers are on the state exemption list too.

Before choosing an asking price, call the Lancaster County Recorder of Deeds for the full transfer tax on your deed, school district share included.

The county's Property Assessment Office covers more than 195,000 parcels in 60 municipalities and 17 school districts. Its previous reassessment took effect January 1, 2018, at market value on that date and a 100 percent ratio. The next, for 2027, is in progress, and during 2025 and 2026 assessors may inspect from outside and photograph exteriors.

The purpose is to even out values between properties, not to raise money. Taxing bodies have to lower their rates to stay revenue neutral, so a bigger assessment on your house is not the same as a bigger bill. Buyers will still set your assessed value beside similar houses.

  • Yearly appeals must be in by August 1.
  • In a reassessment year the window is 40 days from the date on the notice.
  • Once 2027 is over, the following yearly appeal chance is 2028.
  • A three-member Board of Assessment Appeals hears them.

No form freezes or eliminates property taxes for seniors, so disregard any video or mailer that claims one does. Call the Assessment Office at 717-299-8381 to learn about the programs that do exist.

The township has a Building Code Official who reviews permits and carries out inspections, plus an inspector for property maintenance. Code Administrators Inc. performs inspections and needs 24 hours' notice. Residents can also file code enforcement complaints and request records research.

Before listing, dig out permits and final inspection records for any deck, finished basement or new furnace. It is simpler to settle gaps with the township while the house is still yours. One generic form covers residential building and zoning, another covers commercial work, and the zoning map is online. If a buyer questions an old addition, a records research request shows what the township holds.

sections.h2: Selling a rental or an inherited house
sections.html:
If tenants live in the house, tell the buyer early and share the lease and rent history. Showings follow the lease terms, so plan the schedule with the tenant. For an inherited house, the title company will want proof of who can sign for the estate before it prepares the deed. The township's transfer tax ordinance exempts a transfer to an heir from a decedent, but the later sale to a buyer is taxable.

In either case, settle open items with the township first. A permit that was never closed, or a property maintenance complaint, is easier to resolve before a buyer finds it during a title search.

A listing suits a house in good condition inside a well-regarded school district. An as-is sale fits an estate, a house needing major repairs, a rental with a difficult tenant, or a move that cannot wait on showings and a buyer's financing. Weigh offers by what remains after transfer tax, any unpaid tax, prorated school and county bills and repair credits. Insist that offers come in writing.

With a cash buyer there is no mortgage approval, no lender appraisal and no financing contingency, which removes the usual reasons a closing slips. You also skip staging, repeated showings and repair requests after an inspection. The paperwork on your side stays the same: tax certification, transfer tax at recording, and any open permit or tax balance.

For an estate house, a vacant property or a tenant problem, that trade can justify a lower price. Ask every buyer how much time they need, who pays for title work and recording, and whether they will accept the house as it stands.

1. Email the tax certification request and mail the $25 check.
  2. Call the Recorder of Deeds to learn the combined transfer tax.
  3. Gather permits and final inspections for work done on the house.
  4. Ask your lender for a payoff if a mortgage is open.
  5. Confirm the settlement date with the title company and the buyer.

A cash buyer has no lender timeline, so this list usually moves faster than it would in a financed sale. Add one more habit: keep copies of everything you send, because a lost envelope can cost days.

faqs.q: Is East Hempfield part of the City of Lancaster?
faqs.a: No. East Hempfield is a separate township in Lancaster County, though it shares the Lancaster mailing designation with five other suburbs. Permits and zoning come from the township.

faqs.q: Who collects school taxes on an East Hempfield house?
faqs.a: The Hempfield School District sends its own bill at 19.8786 mills for 2026-27. County and township taxes go through the Lancaster County Treasurer.

faqs.q: How do I get a tax certification for an East Hempfield closing?
faqs.a: Email the Lancaster County Tax Collection Bureau with the owner name, address, 13-digit parcel number and settlement date, and mail a $25 check payable to LCTCB Real Estate Tax Group.

faqs.q: What is the appeal window for my East Hempfield assessment?
faqs.a: Annual appeals are due by August 1. In a reassessment year, you have 40 days from the notice date. After the 2027 reassessment, the next annual appeal opportunity is 2028.

faqs.q: Does the township require an inspection before I sell?
faqs.a: Its code office handles permit review, inspections through Code Administrators Inc. and code enforcement. Call the code office before you list to learn whether anything further applies to your address.
